evidence.note: Compiler built via a few large apply_patch operations right after cargo init, rather than an ordered progression of feature milestones each with a done-signal — resembles a big-bang build.
The only progress check used is the full bash /app/run_tests.sh (all 780 tests); no per-milestone test subsets are run to certify individual features/stages.

Debugging is reactive feature-to-feature: pick a specific failing program (page_boundary, unroll-1, 20001121-1, 20010129-1), read it, patch, rebuild, rerun full suite — no dependency-ordered sequencing or completion criteria.

Extensive upfront reading of harness and sample tests shows orientation, but this never translates into an explicit staged milestone plan; no TodoWrite or feature-ordering artifact appears anywhere in the trajectory.

reasoning: The observed behavior is a large up-front build followed by reactive, feature-to-feature debugging against the full 780-test suite, with no explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan, no per-milestone success checks, and no test-subset checkpoints — the only done-signal is the whole suite. This sits between anchor 0 ('works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria') and anchor 3 ('a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing'), landing at 2, with the targeting of individual failing programs being the only weak gesture toward feature-level structure.
